subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Nudges and System 1 Thinking
description: One-minute skill: Nudges and System 1 Thinking.

hook.text: You see a green arrow on the floor pointing toward the exit. You follow it without thinking.

buildup.text: System 1 is fast, automatic, and effortless. System 2 is slow, deliberate, and costly. Most decisions are System 1.

discovery.text: Nudges target System 1. They work with the brain's shortcuts, not against them. That's why they're so effective.

twist.text: Education targets System 2: 'think carefully about your choices.' But people have limited System 2 capacity.

climax.text: The best nudge is invisible. It makes the right choice feel obvious before you've even realized you're choosing.

punchline.text: Work with the brain, not against it.

quiz.question: Which thinking system do nudges primarily target?
options: Neither; nudges work on pure logic

details.summary: Nudges work because they operate on System 1, the fast, automatic, and intuitive mode of thinking. By changing defaults, framing, and environmental cues, nudges redirect automatic behavior without requiring the effortful deliberation of System 2 analytical thinking.
details.whyItMatters: Most daily decisions are made by System 1 on autopilot. Nudges are effective precisely because they influence decisions at the automatic level rather than requiring people to engage slow, effortful analysis.
takeaways: Nudges primarily influence fast, automatic System 1 thinking
System 1 responds to defaults, framing, salience, and social cues
Information campaigns target System 2 but most decisions are made by System 1

faq.question: Why do nudges work when informational approaches often fail?
faq.answer: Information targets System 2 deliberate thinking, but most behavior is governed by System 1 automatic processing. People may know they should save more, eat healthier, or exercise, but System 1 follows the path of least resistance. Nudges change that path.

faq.question: Can nudges also work through System 2 thinking?
faq.answer: Some nudges, like simplified information disclosure, work by making System 2 engagement easier. But the most powerful nudges, defaults, environmental design, and framing, work because they steer System 1 without requiring any deliberation at all.
